text:
acme_infra: Hey, we're seeing a bunch of 429s during our demo this morning. Started around 09:20 PT, spikes when 50 concurrent users hit /v1/generate. sample response: 
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 3

acme_infra: Repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-123" -d '{"model":"redwood-small","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}' --parallel 50 (python spawn). Happens consistently every 5-10s when we scale up.

jess_support: ugh, thanks for the details. I pulled your org (acme-inc) — looks like you're on the Free tier cap (burst concurrency 60, daily token cap 100k). That explains the X-RateLimit headers.

jess_support: quick Qs: are those 50 distinct API keys or a single shared key? also do you have client-side retries/backoff configured?

acme_infra: single key, we were assuming the free plan would allow a short demo burst. No sophisticated backoff, basic retry. Demo is for customers in 30m.

mike_eng: fyi, the Retry-After semantics are enforced by our gateway. If a single key hits concurrency cap the gateway returns 429 until concurrent slots free. Workarounds: 1) queue + exponential backoff 2) reduce concurrency per client 3) use streaming with smaller chunks 4) request temporary uplift.

mike_eng: also you can enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts to drop token usage quickly if prompts are identical.

jess_support: I can provision a 24h temporary uplift to avoid the 429s for the demo, but we need a quick approval from sales/billing for billing/abuse checks. Ana, can you take?

ana_sales: @jess_support I'm on it. acme_infra, I'll need company name + approximate monthly usage after demo + billing contact. Can you paste the org_id and the last 12h of request IDs?

acme_infra: org_id: org_acme_77. Recent request ids: req_08a3, req_08a4, req_08a5 (one example log line): 
[2024-06-15T16:22:14Z] req_08a4 POST /v1/generate 429 sk-acme-123

jess_support: thanks. I'll open a temporary exception ticket: "TB-1829" and set expiry 24h from now. billing-bot: can you create and attach the temporary uplift record to acme-inc with reason "demo surge"?

billing-bot: Created uplift TB-1829 — +100 concurrent slots for 24h, expires 2024-06-16T17:22:00Z. Pending final invoice reconciliation.

acme_infra: awesome, testing now... sending 70 parallel requests...

acme_infra: looks good, no 429s now. thanks! latency sits around 420ms p95 which is fine for demo.

jess_support: great. A couple of follow-ups: 1) please implement exponential backoff and retry-after handling (our SDKs do this by default) 2) consider an upgrade to the Starter plan if your post-demo usage will be sustained — it has higher burst caps + SLA 3) use separate keys per client/seat to avoid single-key throttles.

mike_eng: for long term, if you need predictable throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated or a Reserved capacity seat; we can run a quick cost/latency calc if you share typical concurrency and tokens/day.

ana_sales: pinging billing for the formal invoice adjust and note: will follow up with a sales quote if they plan >50k tokens/mo.

acme_infra: thanks everyone. Quick doc request — can you send the uplift request template and the SDK backoff snippet?

jess_support: putting links: https://redwood.ai/docs/limits and https://github.com/redwood-ai/sdk/blob/main/examples/retry.md

jess_support: closing the thread for now since TB-1829 is active. Reopen if you see more 429s after uplift expires. :thumbsup:
